days.title: Nail Anatomy
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Learn the nail plate, cuticle, matrix and free edge so you never damage the nail.

video.title: One Bead Acrylic Application Tutorial

steps: Get your tools ready: nail file, cuticle pusher and acrylic brush.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: The matrix is where the nail grows from and must never be damaged.

Learn the parts of the nail: the nail plate (the hard part you see), the cuticle (the skin at the base), the matrix (where the nail grows from) and the free edge (the tip that sticks out) so you never damage the nail. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise nail anatomy on a model or a practice head. Learn the parts of the nail: the nail plate (the hard part you see), the cuticle (the skin at the base), the matrix (where the nail grows from) and the free edge (the tip that sticks out) so you never damage the nail. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do nail anatomy two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: What is the key point of today's lesson on nail anatomy?
options: The best result comes from skipping the preparation step.
You never need to check your work until the very end.
The matrix is where the nail grows from and must never be damaged.
Using dirty tools gives the same result as clean ones.
quiz.explain: The matrix is where the nail grows from and must never be damaged.

quiz.q: Which tool is most essential for nail anatomy?

quiz.q: What should you always do when working on nail anatomy?
